bib.title: Sharp Nearby, Fuzzy Far Away: How Neural Language Models Use Context

read.skipped: Appendices A (hyperparameters) and B (extra figures) are referenced but absent from the PDF text; figure contents not readable as text.

question: How much prior context does an LSTM language model use, and are nearby and distant context represented differently, and how do copy mechanisms help?
contributions: Test-time ablations (truncate, shuffle/reverse, replace, drop) of context in a trained LSTM LM
Effective context about 200 tokens; nearby (50 tokens) vs long-range split
Analysis of how the neural cache helps copying from distant context

method.summary: Take a standard AWD-LSTM LM trained normally, and at test time perturb the prior context (truncate, permute, drop, replace) and measure the increase in dev NLL/perplexity. Also compare with and without a neural cache on words copyable from nearby, far, or no context.

models.name: AWD-LSTM
models.architecture: LSTM LM, trained and finetuned with Averaging SGD

other.hyperparameters: in Appendix A, not in extracted text

other.note: Model is not trained with perturbations. Varied one at a time: BPTT timesteps, dropout rate, model size (hidden, layers, embedding).

metrics.name: NLL / perplexity
metrics.definition: PP = exp(NLL) on held-out dev; ablations reported as increase in NLL or relative perplexity

baselines: random-drop control of same token count
eval.protocol: Dev sets only; test results said to be consistent; mean of 3 seeds, error bars std (Fig 1,2) or 95% CI (Fig 3,4,7).

results.claim: Effective context size is about 200 tokens
results.setup: Averaging-SGD LSTM LM (Merity 2018), dev sets, mean of 3 seeds, PTB and Wiki
results.quote:
we ﬁnd that the model is capable of using about 200 to-
kens of context on average

results.claim: 1% perplexity increase only beyond 150 tokens on PTB and 250 on Wiki
results.setup: Averaging-SGD LSTM LM (Merity 2018), dev sets, mean of 3 seeds
results.quote:
we only see a 1% increase in perplexity as we
move beyond a context of 150 tokens on PTB and
250 tokens on Wiki

results.claim: Local word order matters only within the 20 most recent tokens
results.setup: Averaging-SGD LSTM LM (Merity 2018), dev sets, mean of 3 seeds, span of 20 tokens, n=300
results.quote:
Local word order only matters for the most re-
cent 20 tokens

results.claim: Global word order matters only within the 50 most recent tokens
results.setup: Averaging-SGD LSTM LM (Merity 2018), dev sets, mean of 3 seeds, n=300
results.quote:
Global order of words only matters for the most
recent 50 tokens

results.claim: Dropping content words 5 tokens away raises perplexity by about 65% vs 17% for random drop
results.setup: Averaging-SGD LSTM LM (Merity 2018), dev sets, mean of 3 seeds, PTB, s1=5, n=300

results.claim: For Cfar words, dropping all distant context raises perplexity 12% vs 2% for dropping target occurrences
results.setup: Averaging-SGD LSTM LM (Merity 2018), dev sets, mean of 3 seeds, PTB

results.claim: For Cnear words dropping the target raises perplexity almost 9% vs about 3.5% for dropping long-range context
results.setup: Averaging-SGD LSTM LM (Merity 2018), dev sets, mean of 3 seeds, PTB
results.quote:
removing the target word which increases perplexity by
almost 9%

results.claim: Without a cache, Cfar words see 53% perplexity increase on Wiki vs 32% for Cnear
results.setup: Averaging-SGD LSTM LM (Merity 2018), dev sets, mean of 3 seeds, Wiki, cache size 3,875

results.claim: Cache hurts about 36% of PTB words (and 20% of Wiki) that cannot be copied from context
results.quote:
the cache also hurts about 36% of
the words in PTB and 20% in Wiki

results.claim: 13-token context gives 25% perplexity increase in this setup vs about 8% reported by Chelba et al.
results.setup: Averaging-SGD LSTM LM (Merity 2018), dev sets, mean of 3 seeds, PTB, 13 tokens
results.quote:
compared to a 25% increase at 13 tokens of con-
text in our setup
results.note: Authors attribute gap to Chelba training with restricted context

limits: Perturbations applied only at test time; model not trained on them, so losses are upper bounds.
Single architecture (AWD-LSTM) and two small datasets; model and data effects are confounded (vocab, dataset size).
Token-level analysis only; sentence-level interactions left to future work.
Results on dev sets only; hyperparameters in Appendix A not in the extracted text.
Pre-Transformer; does not cover attention models.

terms.definition: number of tokens that achieve a similar loss (1-2% perplexity difference) to infinite context
target words copyable from the 50 most recent tokens, only from beyond 50 tokens, or not at all
